Name: Aggressive Auto Connect Upgrade
Description:
[h2]Aggressive Auto Connect Upgrade[/h2]

Ever rebuilt a critical section of your ship under fire, only to discover that half the equipment is still sitting there politely waiting for electricity? Well, have I got an unnecessarily forceful solution for you!

Here at Aggressive Auto Connect Upgrade (Inc.), we believe electrical devices should stop being shy and introduce themselves to the grid. Enable the system, choose how aggressively it should check the ship (five seconds by default), and watch connectable equipment get shoved back into productive society.

And if polite introductions are not enough, version 1.1 adds an optional solution with all the subtlety of flipping the breaker off and back on again.

Version 1.2 also adds an optional answer for colonists having a Lights Out mental breakdown: AACU can switch their chosen device back on before the rest of the crew notices.

[h2]What It Does[/h2]

While enabled, Aggressive Auto Connect Upgrade periodically asks Stardeus's current Auto Connect planner whether useful electrical work exists. If Core produces a legal plan, AACU invokes Stardeus's own [b]Try Auto Connect[/b] operation.

Normal pulses preserve vanilla electrical-grid rules. Core owns nearest-connector selection, Ship Computer limits, switched-off Switch boundaries, and the final connection operation. Isolated devices and buildings that Core cannot legally connect do not cause pointless pulses.

[h2]Features[/h2]

[h3]Aggressive Reconnection[/h3]
- Uses a configurable pulse interval, defaulting to five seconds
- Invokes vanilla Try Auto Connect only when Core's current planner finds useful work
- Preserves Core's nearest-connector, Ship Computer limit, and switched-off Switch rules
- Ignores isolated devices that Core cannot currently connect
- Requires the vanilla Auto Connect Upgrade to be installed in a Ship Computer

[h3]Complete Grid Reconnect[/h3]
- Optional and disabled by default
- Detects buildings that still have an electrical connection but cannot reach a Ship Computer
- Can also recover a constructed zero-link connector when every compatible powered-grid connector in range is full
- Requires a movable existing device link and enough connector capacity to produce a net connection gain
- Activates only for a legal stranded-device recovery or a verified full-connector rebalance
- Confirms the same legal recovery candidate across two pulses before full teardown
- Uses Core's bulk grid teardown, retains stale-state recovery, and performs a complete vanilla reconnection
- Prevents overlapping reconnect operations and finishes eligible connections in one controlled operation
- Prevents another full reconnect until the previous recovery condition clears
- Defers full electrical teardown while entering or traveling through hyperspace, including warp-drive jumps

[h3]Lights Out Recovery[/h3]
- Optional and disabled by default
- Restores devices switched off by a colonist during the Lights Out mental breakdown
- Leaves player-controlled and other shutdowns untouched
- Operates independently of automatic connection pulses

[h3]Persistent Controls[/h3]
- Adds a compact status widget immediately beside the top-bar electricity display
- Cooperatively positions the widget alongside compatible mod controls
- Uses distinct enabled and disabled icons for quick status recognition
- Click the widget to open or close the settings panel
- Set the pulse interval from 0.25 to 3600 seconds
- Assign or clear a persistent keyboard shortcut
- Toggle automatic connection pulses from either the panel or shortcut

[h2]Important Behavior[/h2]

Normal aggressive reconnection may connect equipment to any grid that vanilla Try Auto Connect considers valid. This is especially useful during combat, when restoring power matters more than preserving a carefully separated network.

[b]Complete Grid Reconnect is intentionally more forceful.[/b] When enabled and its recovery condition is detected, it disconnects and rebuilds the electrical network. This can override carefully arranged or Switch-controlled subgrids. Leave this option disabled if preserving those grids is more important than recovering stranded equipment.

Complete Grid Reconnect requires the same legal recovery candidate to remain across two automatic pulses. After one full rebuild, it will not run again until the recovery condition clears. This gives normal construction and connection restoration time to settle without repeated grid-wide operations.

A full-connector rebalance is considered only for a constructed connector with no links, after Core finds no ordinary solution, when every compatible powered-grid connector in range is full. AACU also verifies that an existing device link can move to the isolated connector and that the connector will retain additional capacity after its grid uplink and moved device. Switched-off Switch boundaries remain protected.

To avoid interrupting powered engines, Complete Grid Reconnect is deferred while the ship is entering or traveling through hyperspace; this includes warp-drive jumps. Normal reconnection pulses continue, and a still-needed complete reconnect can run after travel ends.

Lights Out Recovery is a separate, disabled-by-default option. It restores a device only after Core's Lights Out mental breakdown switches it off. Player-controlled and other shutdowns remain untouched, and the recovery does not depend on automatic connection pulses being enabled.

Turn automatic pulses off before manually rearranging electrical grids. Once enabled again, AACU resumes checking for valid recovery opportunities.

[h2]Game Compatibility[/h2]

Requires Stardeus v0.15.0-rc322 or later. AACU uses the rewritten Core Auto Connect planner and its one-frame bulk connection operation.

[h2]Framework Compatibility[/h2]

Tested with Auto Utilities Mod Framework 1.4.0. AACU uses AUMF's stable widget, panel, and shortcut services and does not require the optional custom Theme-Aware UI helpers. Existing controls retain their AUMF-managed theme compatibility without changing AACU's reconnect behavior.

[h2]In Short[/h2]

You built it. A socket can reach it. The upgrade is installed.

[b]It is getting connected.[/b]
